question.prompt: A rectangular sports field has a total distance of exactly 20 metres all the way around its outside edge, which is always twice (that is, 2 times) the sum of its length and width. One pair of opposite sides each measures 4 metres. What is the length of each of the other two sides, in metres?

visuals.altText: Rectangle with one labelled side of 4 metres; the other side length is unknown.

question.explanation: The perimeter of a rectangle equals twice the sum of its length and width. Halving 20 metres gives 10 metres for one length plus one width. One side is already known to measure 4 metres, so subtracting 4 from 10 leaves 6 metres. So each of the other two sides measures 6 metres.
